chiefdom.name: Chiefdom
chiefdom.flavor: Whoever speaks last at the fire, speaks for all.

councilOfElders.name: Council of Elders
councilOfElders.flavor: Slow counsel, and no one hanged for it.

warChief.name: War Chief
warChief.flavor: The spear chooses; the rest agree.

republic.name: Republic
republic.flavor: A crowd that learned to sign its name.
republic.text: +1 culture for each 5 population in a city. −5% happiness demanded per citizen.

tyranny.name: Tyranny
tyranny.flavor: One will, and the roads run straight.

theocracy.name: Theocracy
theocracy.flavor: Law is what the altar remembers.
theocracy.text: +2 faith in every city. Your capital's faith is gained again as science and as culture, at a tenth of the rate.

merchantLeague.name: Merchant League
merchantLeague.flavor: Every treaty has a ledger underneath.
merchantLeague.text: +1 gold for each building that produces gold. Trade routes pay 50% more.

imperium.name: Imperium
imperium.flavor: The map is a claim; the legion is the proof.

theEstates.name: The Estates
theEstates.flavor: Three orders, one hall, and the hall keeps the minutes.
theEstates.text: +1 happiness in every city. +2 culture in every city of 8 or more population.

theSultanate.name: The Sultanate
theSultanate.flavor: The road is short for those the Sultan sends.
theSultanate.text: All units +1 movement, and cities put 25% more production behind units — a fifth off their price. Captured cities +10% science and +10% culture.

theCuria.name: The Curia
theCuria.flavor: What is written in the register is what heaven remembers.
theCuria.text: +3 faith for each Cathedral. Faith buildings supply science equal to their faith.
theCuria.note: There is no cathedral in the game yet — the temple is the last of the faith buildings — so the first clause waits on one.
deferred: +3 faith per Cathedral

theCommonwealth.name: The Commonwealth
theCommonwealth.flavor: The estate is common; the ledger is not.
theCommonwealth.text: Great people may be bought with gold. Great-person improvements pay +50% more.

theEmpire.name: The Empire
theEmpire.flavor: One frontier, and it is wherever the last courier stopped.
theEmpire.text: +6 authority capacity. +1 combat strength for each great general you have earned this game.

theMagisterium.name: The Magisterium
theMagisterium.flavor: The Magister does not rule. He sets the rules.
theMagisterium.text: Every offer of every kind shows one more card. +3 renown per turn for each wonder you hold.

hermitCrown.name: The Hermit Crown
hermitCrown.flavor: A small kingdom, held entirely in one hand.
hermitCrown.text: While you hold at most 4 cities: +30% to every yield in your capital.

riverKings.name: River Kings
riverKings.flavor: The river gives; the dry land is told to be grateful.
riverKings.text: +30% food in every city on fresh water; −10% food and −10% production in every city without it.

woodwrights.name: The Woodwrights
woodwrights.flavor: A forest is a city that has not been felled yet.
woodwrights.text: Clearing a forest or jungle pays +100% and grants +10 culture.

greatLitany.name: The Great Litany
greatLitany.flavor: Say it every day and it becomes true.
greatLitany.text: +1 culture for each 3 faith you gain per turn.

greatWarringTribes.name: The Great Warring Tribes
greatWarringTribes.flavor: No writ runs faster than a horse.
greatWarringTribes.text: Negative authority no longer slows production toward units · +10% production toward mounted units · captured cities pay +5 science and +5 culture.
greatWarringTribes.note: The clause about courthouses does nothing: there is no courthouse in the game yet.

wolfMothersPact.name: Wolf-Mother's Pact
wolfMothersPact.flavor: We are not their prey. We are their kin, and they take their share.
wolfMothersPact.text: Barbarians you kill join you at full health.

athenaeumOfTheRoad.name: Athenaeum of the Road
athenaeumOfTheRoad.flavor: Everything found is kept. Everything kept is known.
athenaeumOfTheRoad.text: A ruin you claim pays every option instead of one.
athenaeumOfTheRoad.note: Retired: this Doctrine is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

foundersRoad.name: The Founders' Road
foundersRoad.flavor: The first stone of every town is a monument to the road that brought it.
foundersRoad.text: Newly founded cities are joined to your nearest city by road · +1 culture in every city.

thalassocracy.name: Thalassocracy
thalassocracy.flavor: Our borders are wherever the tide reaches.
thalassocracy.text: Coastal cities gain 10% of their food yield as gold.

mountainHold.name: Mountain Hold
mountainHold.flavor: The peaks are a wall nobody had to build.
mountainHold.text: +15% production in every city beside a mountain · +5 city defence there.
deferred: the bonus reaching a city with a mountain two hexes away, rather than only one
mountainHold.note: Retired: this Doctrine is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. It was built for a mountain **next to** the city, where the ratified text said within two hexes.

theSacredPath.name: The Sacred Path
theSacredPath.flavor: The old road runs under the trees, and it was not we who laid it.
theSacredPath.text: +1 faith on every forest hex · +1 culture on every jungle hex.

burningWay.name: The Burning Way
burningWay.flavor: Ash is faster than a plough.
burningWay.text: Clearing a forest or jungle costs no worker charge.
deferred: +1 food on every hex you have cleared of forest or jungle
burningWay.note: Not built: the board does not remember a clearing. A felled forest leaves bare ground that looks exactly like ground nothing ever grew on, so nothing can tell the two apart to pay for one of them.

breadAndCircuses.name: Bread and Circuses
breadAndCircuses.flavor: Feed them, amuse them, and they will sing for you.
breadAndCircuses.text: While your authority is positive: +3 happiness in every city of 6 or more population. −2 gold in every city, always.

theTithe.name: The Tithe
theTithe.flavor: A tenth of the harvest, and the gods keep the books.
theTithe.text: +1 gold for each faith you gain per turn.

divineInspiration.name: Divine Inspiration
divineInspiration.text: +1% science and +1% culture for each 200 banked faith.
divineInspiration.note: Faith income today rarely reaches 200 banked faith, so this pays little until faith yields grow.

ironPrice.name: The Iron Price
ironPrice.flavor: Every death a verse; every verse a debt paid.
ironPrice.text: Killing a unit grants +15 culture · pillaging pays +15 gold.

manifestOfTheSteppe.name: Manifest of the Steppe
manifestOfTheSteppe.flavor: There is always more land. There is never enough rest.
manifestOfTheSteppe.text: Settlers cost 40% less to train and have +2 movement · every city demands +1 happiness.

gildedCourt.name: The Gilded Court
gildedCourt.flavor: Gold on the walls, gold in the words, gold under the throne.
gildedCourt.text: Unlocks the Gilded Hall, a building that is bought with gold and never built. +1 science and +1 culture on every hex that yields gold. +1 authority capacity.

grandBazaar.name: The Grand Bazaar
grandBazaar.flavor: The second silk is not nothing. The tenth is a fortune.
grandBazaar.text: Happiness from unique luxuries +50%. A second or later copy of a luxury pays 30% of its bonus instead of nothing. +2 gold for each unique luxury.

masterOfMaps.name: Master of Maps
masterOfMaps.flavor: We see everything. We fear it a little.
masterOfMaps.text: All units +1 sight and +1 movement · all units −2 combat strength.

hegemony.name: Hegemony
hegemony.flavor: Every city carries its own weight, and the crown carries none.
hegemony.text: +1 authority capacity for each city you hold · a captured city costs one less authority.

paxImperia.name: Pax Imperia
paxImperia.flavor: In great cities the noise itself is a kind of peace.
paxImperia.text: +3 happiness and +3 culture in every city of 8 or more population.

religiousMandate.name: Religious Mandate
religiousMandate.flavor: There is one truth, and we are its army.
religiousMandate.text: Permanent war with empires of a different majority religion · your cities cannot be converted.
religiousMandate.note: None of this is built, and the card is never offered.
deferred: permanent war with empires of another faith
your cities cannot be converted
a powerful bonus toward the domination and religious beads

theAcademyOfDeeds.name: The Academy
theAcademyOfDeeds.flavor: A deed unrecorded is a deed undone.
theAcademyOfDeeds.text: −10% culture and +20% science. Great scholar drafts can be bought with faith.

theStandingArmy.name: The Standing Army
theStandingArmy.flavor: The army does not go home. That is the whole of the doctrine.
theStandingArmy.text: +1 authority capacity for each 5 units you have in the field. −1 happiness in every city. Units cost no upkeep.

theSeaCharter.name: The Sea Charter
theSeaCharter.flavor: Sign here, and the tide is yours.
theSeaCharter.text: Trade routes pay 50% more. Every coastal city is founded with a Harbour.
theSeaCharter.note: There is no Harbour in the game yet, so no city is founded with one.
deferred: every coastal city is founded with a Harbour

theRenaissanceCourt.name: The Renaissance Court
theRenaissanceCourt.flavor: Patronage is the cheapest thing a prince ever bought.
theRenaissanceCourt.text: Great-person offers show one more card. Every great person's legacy is 50% stronger.
theRenaissanceCourt.note: Nothing yet makes a legacy stronger, so only the extra card is in effect.
deferred: every great person's legacy is 50% stronger

cuiusRegio.name: Cuius Regio
cuiusRegio.flavor: Whose realm, his religion; whose religion, his realm.
cuiusRegio.text: In cities that follow your religion, 15% of the faith they gain is gained again as science.

theYeomanry.name: The Yeomanry
theYeomanry.flavor: A man with forty acres argues with the tax collector.
theYeomanry.text: +1 production on every hex with a Farm. Cities of 10 or more population −1 happiness.

absolutism.name: Absolutism
absolutism.flavor: The council still meets. It meets to agree.
absolutism.text: +6 authority capacity. A newly placed Order is locked for 10 turns instead of 5.
absolutism.note: The extra slot is not built: a government's slots are laid out when it is adopted, and adding one is a change to that layout rather than a number.
deferred: you gain a wildcard Order slot

blitz.name: Blitz
blitz.flavor: Stop only when there is nothing left in front of you.
blitz.text: Units that kill may move again that turn. Units cannot fortify.
blitz.note: Neither half is built: nothing gives a unit its movement back for a kill, and nothing stops a unit fortifying.
deferred: units that kill may move again that turn
units cannot fortify

thePhilosophersStone.name: The Philosopher's Stone
thePhilosophersStone.flavor: Lead is only gold that has not been asked properly.
thePhilosophersStone.text: The Great Work costs −25% production. Every Distillery pays +5 gold.
thePhilosophersStone.note: Neither the Great Work project nor the Distillery is in the game yet.
deferred: the Great Work costs −25% production
every Distillery mints +5 gold

theGrandTourII.name: The Grand Tour
theGrandTourII.flavor: One goes to see them, and comes back having been seen.
theGrandTourII.text: +3 renown per turn for each wonder you hold. +1 culture for each wonder in the world, seen or not.

mareNostrum.name: Mare Nostrum
mareNostrum.flavor: They call it a sea. We call it the middle of the country.
mareNostrum.text: +1 food and +1 gold on every water hex you own. Coastal cities cost no authority.

theLeveeEnMasse.name: The Levée en Masse
theLeveeEnMasse.flavor: Every hearth owes a son, and the ledger remembers which.
theLeveeEnMasse.text: When an enemy unit enters your borders, every city with a Barracks musters a militia unit (at most once every 10 turns).
theLeveeEnMasse.note: Not built: nothing in the game happens when a foreign unit crosses your border.
deferred: cities with a Barracks muster a militia when an enemy enters your borders

paxMagistri.name: Pax Magistri
paxMagistri.flavor: The long quiet, and the accounts that grew in it.
paxMagistri.text: +3 happiness in every city. +5 science and +5 culture in every city of 12 or more population.
paxMagistri.note: The clause about declaring war is not built: empires are not yet at war or at peace.
deferred: you can no longer declare war

theEncyclopaedia.name: The Encyclopaedia
theEncyclopaedia.flavor: Everything, in order, by somebody who never left the room.
theEncyclopaedia.text: +1 science for each building in a city. Science buildings cost −50% production.

theGentleYoke.name: The Gentle Yoke
theGentleYoke.flavor: Ask little of them and they will not notice the asking.
theGentleYoke.text: −15% happiness demanded per citizen · every city costs 2 more authority.
theGentleYoke.note: The extra authority is asked of every city you hold, not only of the ones you found after taking this Doctrine.
deferred: asking the extra authority only of the cities you found after taking this Doctrine

theScatteredHearths.name: The Scattered Hearths
theScatteredHearths.flavor: A hamlet of three keeps itself. A capital of thirty does not.
theScatteredHearths.text: The first 3 citizens in every city demand no happiness · −4 happiness in your capital.

theWanderingCourt.name: The Wandering Court
theWanderingCourt.flavor: The court sleeps where it stops, and the country is the better for it.
theWanderingCourt.text: −15% to every yield in your capital · +3 food, production, science, culture and faith, and +3 happiness, in every city but your capital.

theClosedRealm.name: The Closed Realm
theClosedRealm.flavor: The gate is shut. What is inside it is enough.
theClosedRealm.text: Your happiness is fixed at +5, always · your units cannot attack outside your territory.
deferred: your happiness is held at +5 whatever your cities ask for
your units cannot attack outside your own territory
theClosedRealm.note: Not built, both halves. Nothing in this game can hold a meter at a number instead of adding to it, and nothing can refuse an attack for where it is being made.

theTriumphalWay.name: The Triumphal Way
theTriumphalWay.flavor: The road into the city was widened once, for one afternoon, four hundred years ago.
theTriumphalWay.text: Capturing a city grants +5 happiness in every city for 10 turns.

bloodedSpears.name: Blooded Spears
bloodedSpears.flavor: The wild taught us. We took notes.
bloodedSpears.text: +1 combat strength, and +2 more against barbarians.

campFollowers.name: Camp Followers
campFollowers.text: Clearing a barbarian camp grants +25 food and a random military unit.

farRunners.name: Far Runners
farRunners.flavor: Run until the land is new, then run once more.
farRunners.text: Scouts +1 movement and +1 sight. Civilians +2 movement while embarked.

theLongWatch.name: The Long Watch
theLongWatch.flavor: A sleepless wall is a comfort to those inside it.
theLongWatch.text: +1 happiness for each unit standing in one of your cities, and +1 more for each fortification a city has built.

theWidowsLevy.name: The Widow's Levy
theWidowsLevy.text: When a unit of yours dies, its nearest city gains +10 production and you gain +40 gold.

militiaLevies.name: Militia Levies
militiaLevies.flavor: Every farmer a spear, every roof a watchtower.
militiaLevies.text: All your cities gain +4 defense and +1 sight radius.

commonGranary.name: Common Granary
commonGranary.flavor: One store, one hunger, one answer.
commonGranary.text: +1 food in every city holding an improved luxury resource.

saltTithes.name: Salt Tithes
saltTithes.flavor: Salt is small. Its tax is not.

boundaryStones.name: Boundary Stones
boundaryStones.flavor: A stone that says *ours* says it forever.
boundaryStones.note: Border expansion is how fast a city claims its next hex, fed by that city’s own culture — separate from the culture your empire saves toward its next draft. This hurries the borders only.

borderBallads.name: Border Ballads
borderBallads.flavor: Fear, set to a tune, becomes a people.
borderBallads.text: +2 culture for each barbarian camp you have found, and +10 culture for each barbarian unit you kill.
borderBallads.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

vanguard.name: Vanguard
vanguard.flavor: Strangers' ground fights harder — so must we.

spoilsOfTheWild.name: Spoils of the Wild
spoilsOfTheWild.flavor: Their plunder was ours all along.

horseLords.name: Horse Lords
horseLords.flavor: The saddle is a country of its own.

weightsAndMeasures.name: Weights & Measures
weightsAndMeasures.flavor: An honest scale is the first tax.

silkRoads.name: Silk Roads
silkRoads.flavor: Rare things travel; travel makes them rarer.
silkRoads.text: +3 gold for each trade route you run.

theSaltRoad.name: The Salt Road
theSaltRoad.flavor: Every field pays a toll on its way to market.
theSaltRoad.text: +1 gold on every hex carrying a strategic resource.
theSaltRoad.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The Golden Scales stands in its place.

theTaxFarm.name: The Tax Farm
theTaxFarm.flavor: Count the people, and the coin counts itself.
theTaxFarm.text: +1 gold for each 4 population in your empire.

harbourDues.name: Harbour Dues
harbourDues.flavor: The sea pays for the privilege of arriving.
harbourDues.text: Coastal cities gain +2 gold and +1 culture.

landGrants.name: Land Grants
landGrants.flavor: Land, given freely, is land that was owed.
landGrants.text: Buying a hex costs 25% less · +40% border expansion.

homesteadCharters.name: Homestead Charters
homesteadCharters.flavor: The wagon holds one more family than the law allows.
homesteadCharters.text: Newly founded cities start with 1 more population.

granaryLevies.name: Granary Levies
granaryLevies.flavor: A new mouth is a new pair of hands.
granaryLevies.text: When a city grows, it gains +10 production.

censusRolls.name: The King's Table
censusRolls.flavor: A place is laid for every mouth in the city, and every mouth knows it.
censusRolls.text: +1 happiness for every 2 citizens in your capital.

tinkersGuild.name: Tinkers' Guild
tinkersGuild.flavor: One more mend in every bag of tools.

publicGranaries.name: Public Granaries
publicGranaries.flavor: The city eats slowly, and stays fed.
publicGranaries.text: Cities keep 15% of their stored food when they grow.

festivalDays.name: Festival Days
festivalDays.flavor: Idleness, made sacred, keeps the peace.

curiousElders.name: Curious Elders
curiousElders.flavor: The old ask questions the young forgot to.
curiousElders.text: +5 science whenever you claim a ruin.
curiousElders.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

ritesOfPassage.name: Rites of Passage
ritesOfPassage.flavor: A sword blessed is a soul enlisted.
ritesOfPassage.text: Buying or completing a unit grants +10 faith.
ritesOfPassage.note: A unit bought with gold counts as completed, so it pays this too — but only once.

theLooseRein.name: The Loose Rein
theLooseRein.flavor: Laws that change quickly are laws that are watched closely.
theLooseRein.text: A newly placed Order is locked for 2 turns instead of 5.
theLooseRein.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

fieldSurgeons.name: Field Surgeons
fieldSurgeons.flavor: Stitched on the road, marching by morning.
fieldSurgeons.text: All units heal +10 more per turn, anywhere.

theShieldWall.name: The Shield Wall
theShieldWall.flavor: High ground and a locked line — the old arithmetic.

siegeDoctrine.name: Siege Doctrine
siegeDoctrine.flavor: Walls are patient. We are less so.

scorchedEarth.name: Scorched Earth
scorchedEarth.flavor: What we cannot keep, we salt.
scorchedEarth.text: Pillaging heals a further 25 and pays a further +10 gold.

sumptuaryLaws.name: Sumptuary Laws
sumptuaryLaws.flavor: Only the crown wears the purple; all the rest are glad to see it.

publicani.name: Publicani
publicani.flavor: The writ has a price, and we collect it.
publicani.text: +2 gold for each point of positive authority.

charteredCompanies.name: Chartered Companies
charteredCompanies.flavor: Every deed of land comes with a survey attached.
charteredCompanies.text: Buying a hex pays +5 science · buying a hex costs 15% less.

foreignQuarters.name: Foreign Quarters
foreignQuarters.flavor: The neighbour's coin spends as well as ours.
foreignQuarters.text: +1 gold and +1 science in every city near another empire's territory.
foreignQuarters.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

oreTithes.name: Ore Tithes
oreTithes.flavor: Where the ore is, the hammers gather.
oreTithes.text: +1 production on every hex carrying a strategic resource.

terracedHillsides.name: Terraced Hillsides
terracedHillsides.flavor: The hill was made to feed us; it only needed steps.

masterMasons.name: Master Masons
masterMasons.flavor: Every finished wall is a song about itself.

royalSurveyors.name: Royal Surveyors
royalSurveyors.flavor: The chain and the plumb line, quietly annexing.
royalSurveyors.text: +50% border expansion · buying a hex costs 25% less.

provincialGovernors.name: Provincial Governors
provincialGovernors.flavor: Distance obeys, if someone is paid to make it.

emergencyPowers.name: Emergency Powers
emergencyPowers.flavor: When the writ tears, the capital holds the pieces.
emergencyPowers.text: While your authority is negative: capital +25% production, and borders do not freeze.

theCommonPurse.name: The Common Purse
theCommonPurse.flavor: Nothing left on the workbench is wasted.
theCommonPurse.text: Leftover production from a completed item is doubled.

pilgrimRoads.name: Pilgrim Roads
pilgrimRoads.flavor: Where the faithful walk, the faithful settle.
pilgrimRoads.text: +1 faith for every 3 citizens in your capital · +1 happiness for each 50 banked faith (at most +5).

lamplighters.name: Lamplighters
lamplighters.flavor: A small flame kept is a small song sung.
lamplighters.text: +1 culture for each 5 faith you gain per turn.

scholarsStipend.name: Scholars' Stipend
scholarsStipend.flavor: A crowd is a library that has not been catalogued.
scholarsStipend.text: +2 science in every city of 5 or more population.

theMarshals.name: The Marshals
theMarshals.flavor: Shoulder to shoulder, the line is one animal.
theMarshals.text: +2 combat strength for each adjacent friendly combat unit (at most +4).

garrisonState.name: Garrison State
garrisonState.flavor: The soldiers do not idle. Nobody does.
garrisonState.text: Each city gains +3 production for each combat unit standing in it (at most +6 per city).

skirmishersCreed.name: Skirmishers' Creed
skirmishersCreed.flavor: Strike from where they cannot answer.

theFinishersArt.name: The Finisher's Art
theFinishersArt.text: +4 combat strength against units below half strength.

frontierForts.name: Frontier Forts
frontierForts.flavor: The border is where we keep our walls.
frontierForts.text: +6 city defence in every city near another empire's territory.

triumphs.name: Triumphs
triumphs.flavor: A city taken is a story told forever.
triumphs.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.
deferred: capturing a city also grants 5 renown

theStandingLevy.name: The Standing Levy
theStandingLevy.flavor: The spear is always first in line.
theStandingLevy.text: Every 12 turns, a free melee unit musters in your capital.

clientKings.name: Client Kings
clientKings.flavor: Better a king who bows than a province that rebels.
clientKings.text: +2 authority capacity · a captured city costs one less authority.

provincialMints.name: Provincial Mints
provincialMints.flavor: Every seam of silk, its own small coin.
provincialMints.text: +2 gold for each improved copy of a luxury — duplicates count.

quarrymensGuild.name: Quarrymen's Guild
quarrymensGuild.text: +4 production in every city with a quarry.

theGrainDole.name: The Grain Dole
theGrainDole.flavor: A full city is a quiet one.
theGrainDole.text: +2 happiness in every city of 6 or more population.

mandateOfHeaven.name: Mandate of Heaven
mandateOfHeaven.flavor: The pious are easy to govern, and they know it.
mandateOfHeaven.text: The science and culture your happy cities pay rises 5 percentage points · +1 happiness for each 200 banked faith.

theLyceum.name: The Lyceum
theLyceum.flavor: Every new thing learned is a song about the old.
theLyceum.text: Completing a technology grants an extra turn of culture.

censusOfSouls.name: Census of Souls
censusOfSouls.flavor: A great city prays in a great voice.
censusOfSouls.text: +1 faith for each citizen in your capital.

tolerationEdicts.name: Toleration Edicts
tolerationEdicts.flavor: Let them keep their gods; they will pay their taxes.

theLaureate.name: The Laureate
theLaureate.flavor: The court keeps one chair empty, and it is never empty for long.
theLaureate.text: +1 renown per turn. Every great-person improvement pays +2 more of its own yield.
theLaureate.note: The great-person improvements are the academy, landmark, manufactory, customs house and citadel.

theLegion.name: The Legion
theLegion.flavor: Ten thousand men who march as one, and dig the ditch as one.
theLegion.text: Melee units gain +1 movement and +1 combat strength, and cities put 15% more production behind them.

fireKeepers.name: Fire-Keepers
fireKeepers.flavor: Someone has sat up with it every night since the first night.
fireKeepers.text: +1 faith in your capital, and +1 happiness there.

wolfRunners.name: Wolf-Runners
wolfRunners.flavor: They come back with the country in their heads.
wolfRunners.text: Scouts gain +1 movement, and claiming a ruin grants +15 gold.
wolfRunners.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

hearthSongs.name: Hearth Songs
hearthSongs.flavor: Small places keep the tunes the big ones forget.
hearthSongs.text: +2 culture in every city of 4 population or less.
hearthSongs.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it. The Harvest Songs stands in its place.

firstFruitsOffering.name: First Fruits
firstFruitsOffering.flavor: The first child of the season is carried to the stone, and given back.
firstFruitsOffering.text: The first citizen born in each city pays +10 faith once.

statuteLabour.name: Statute Labour
statuteLabour.flavor: Every third back is owed to the road.
statuteLabour.text: +1 production in every city for each 4 citizens living there.

riverWardens.name: River Wardens
riverWardens.flavor: The water is watched, so the water is shared.
riverWardens.text: When a unit is standing in one of your cities, that city gains +1 food on every farm beside fresh water.

theAlmanac.name: The Almanac
theAlmanac.flavor: A year written down is a year that can be argued with.
theAlmanac.text: +2 science in your capital, and +1 science in every city with a Library.

villageFairs.name: Village Fairs
villageFairs.flavor: What the second cart carries is bought for pleasure.
villageFairs.text: +1 happiness for each luxury you hold two or more copies of.

theMusterRoll.name: The Muster Roll
theMusterRoll.flavor: The name is written before the man is asked.
theMusterRoll.text: Units created from now on are born with +10 maximum health, and keep it for life.

hillForts.name: Hill Forts
hillForts.flavor: Uphill, every stone is a soldier.
hillForts.text: +2 combat strength when defending on hills, and a city on hills costs 1 less authority.

thePilgrimsPurse.name: The Pilgrim's Purse
thePilgrimsPurse.flavor: Nobody walks that far without stopping to eat.
thePilgrimsPurse.text: +5 faith in every city standing beside a holy site.

charterTowns.name: Charter Towns
charterTowns.flavor: The grain store is written into the charter, above the wall.
charterTowns.text: Newly founded cities are founded with a Granary.

theChoir.name: The Choir
theChoir.flavor: Forty voices, and not one of them heard on its own.
theChoir.text: +1 culture and +1 happiness in every city with a Temple.

starGazers.name: Star-Gazers
starGazers.flavor: Above the smoke, the sky keeps better records.
starGazers.text: +2 science in every city with a mountain hex inside its borders.

cisternWorks.name: Cistern Works
cisternWorks.flavor: The rain of one winter, kept under the square.
cisternWorks.text: Every city of yours counts as standing on fresh water.
cisternWorks.note: It answers what is asked of a city — whether the town can drink. A hex out in the fields is still watered by the river or by nothing.

ledgerKeepers.name: Ledger-Keepers
ledgerKeepers.flavor: The column of figures is longer than the road.
ledgerKeepers.text: +1 gold in every city with a Market, and +1 trade route.

drumsOfWar.name: Drums of War
drumsOfWar.flavor: They learn the step before they learn the spear.
drumsOfWar.text: While this Order is in a slot, units created from now on are born with +2 combat strength, and keep it for life.

theCartographers.name: The Cartographers
theCartographers.flavor: The blank part of the sheet is the part worth paying for.
theCartographers.text: +1 science for each 40 hexes you have revealed.

theMasonsLodge.name: The Masons' Lodge
theMasonsLodge.flavor: A trade that will not teach a stranger keeps its walls straight.
theMasonsLodge.text: Cities of 6 population or more put 10% more production behind buildings.

theOathBound.name: The Oath-Bound
theOathBound.flavor: They swore it over a fire, and the fire is still lit.
theOathBound.text: Killing a unit heals the unit that struck the blow by 15.

sanctuary.name: Sanctuary
sanctuary.flavor: They may take the gate, the granary and the gold. Not the stones.
sanctuary.text: Your holy city cannot be taken while it keeps your religion — it is sacked instead.
deferred: your holy city is sacked rather than captured while it keeps your religion
sanctuary.note: Not built: a city can only be captured in this game, never sacked. Retired until sacking exists.

waysideShrines.name: Wayside Shrines
waysideShrines.flavor: A stone, a bowl, a name. No priest required.

theOrchardTithe.name: The Orchard Tithe
theOrchardTithe.flavor: The tenth basket goes to the crown, and the crown plants it.
theOrchardTithe.text: +1 food on every hex carrying a luxury resource.

theUnbrokenLand.name: The Unbroken Land
theUnbrokenLand.flavor: Nothing was asked of this ground. It gave anyway.
theUnbrokenLand.text: +1 food and +1 production on every unimproved forest or jungle hex.

theGreenwoodLaw.name: The Greenwood Law
theGreenwoodLaw.flavor: The law of the greenwood is short enough to remember: leave it be.
theGreenwoodLaw.text: +2 food and +2 production on every unimproved hex.
theGreenwoodLaw.note: Retired: this Order is no longer offered in a draft. A saved game that already holds it keeps it.

theQuietFields.name: The Quiet Fields
theQuietFields.flavor: No plough, no boundary, no quarrel.
theQuietFields.text: +1 happiness for each unimproved hex your cities work.

theOldWays.name: The Old Ways
theOldWays.flavor: They farmed here once. It has been better since they stopped.
theOldWays.text: The yields of unimproved hexes are doubled.

firstFruits.name: First Fruits
firstFruits.flavor: The first of everything is set aside. The rest feeds us.
firstFruits.text: +1 food on every hex carrying a resource.

theQuartermasters.name: The Quartermasters
theQuartermasters.flavor: An army marches on ledgers. The ledgers march on nothing at all.
theQuartermasters.text: Military units cost 1 less gold in maintenance.

theWarChest.name: The War Chest
theWarChest.flavor: Kept locked, kept counted, kept full. Kept, above all.
theWarChest.text: Military units cost 3 less gold in maintenance.

forcedMarches.name: Forced Marches
forcedMarches.flavor: Sleep is a thing that happens to other armies.
forcedMarches.text: Melee units gain +1 movement, and +2 instead inside your own territory.

theEscortedRoads.name: The Escorted Roads
theEscortedRoads.flavor: The merchants pay for the spears, and the spears pay them back in miles.
deferred: trade routes within 3 hexes of your soldiers cannot be plundered — nothing in the game can say where a route is safe, only what it pays

theLastHunt.name: The Last Hunt
theLastHunt.flavor: They sing the old raids now. Nobody living remembers being afraid.
theLastHunt.text: +2 culture and +2 science for each barbarian camp you have cleared this game.

theSaintsFields.name: The Saints' Fields
theSaintsFields.flavor: Where a great one stopped to think, the ground has been holy ever since.
theSaintsFields.note: The great-person improvements are the academy, landmark, manufactory, customs house and citadel.

theWayhouses.name: The Wayhouses
theWayhouses.flavor: A bed, a fire, and somebody who will listen to where you have been.
theWayhouses.text: +2 gold and +1 culture for each trade route you run.

theProvisioners.name: The Provisioners
theProvisioners.flavor: Nobody notices the grain until the week it does not come.
theProvisioners.text: +1 happiness for each trade route between your own cities.

thePrizeGrounds.name: The Prize Grounds
thePrizeGrounds.flavor: They founded it on the vein and argued about the name for a century.
thePrizeGrounds.text: +2 happiness in every city settled on a luxury resource.

theCensusEternal.name: The Census Eternal
theCensusEternal.flavor: Every soul written down, every year, for ever. The writing is the point.
theCensusEternal.text: +1 science for every 4 citizens in your empire.

theGroundskeepers.name: The Groundskeepers
theGroundskeepers.flavor: Someone has to weed around the monument.
theGroundskeepers.text: +1 food and +1 production on every great-person improvement.
theGroundskeepers.note: The great-person improvements are the academy, landmark, manufactory, customs house and citadel.

theMastersPresence.name: The Master's Presence
theMastersPresence.flavor: He is not often at home. The town works harder anyway, in case.
theMastersPresence.text: +10% to every yield in each city beside a great person's work.
theMastersPresence.note: A city is beside a work when one stands on its own hex or on one of the six touching it. Two works never pay twice.

theWonderFeasts.name: The Wonder-Feasts
theWonderFeasts.flavor: The scaffolding goes up and the ovens do not go out again for a year.
theWonderFeasts.text: +2 food in every city while it is building a wonder · +10% production toward wonders.

theMasterBuilders.name: The Master Builders
theMasterBuilders.flavor: They have built one of everything. The second is always cheaper.
theMasterBuilders.text: The Magnum Opus and cathedrals cost 15% less production.

theShipwrightShores.name: The Shipwright Shores
theShipwrightShores.flavor: A town that smells of pitch is a town with somewhere to be.
theShipwrightShores.text: +1 production in every coastal city · +30% production toward ships there.

theDryDocks.name: The Dry Docks
theDryDocks.flavor: Pull the sea out from under her and you can see what she has been hiding.
theDryDocks.text: +25% production toward ships in every city with a Harbour.
deferred: ships mend completely in a port — a heal that depends on where a piece is standing is a rule about a hex, and healing is a rule about a turn

theWinteringGrounds.name: The Wintering Grounds
theWinteringGrounds.flavor: Home is wherever the horses have stopped.
theWinteringGrounds.text: Your units cost no gold in maintenance outside your territory.

theArchives.name: The Archives
theArchives.flavor: Every law ever passed, in order, in a room nobody is allowed to leave.
theArchives.text: +1 culture for each Order you have placed in a slot.

theAnnalsOfLaw.name: The Annals of Law
theAnnalsOfLaw.flavor: The laws you chose not to pass are also history.
theAnnalsOfLaw.text: +2 culture for each Order you hold but have not placed in a slot.

theAuspiciousSeal.name: The Auspicious Seal
theAuspiciousSeal.flavor: The clerk who chose the day was promoted, and never told anyone why.
theAuspiciousSeal.text: The first time this Order is placed in a slot, a die of the Magister is yours.

theWarCouncil.name: The War Council
theWarCouncil.flavor: Three old soldiers, one map, and a great deal of shouting.
theWarCouncil.text: +1 combat strength for each military Order you have in a slot, at most +3.

theGuildCharter.name: The Guild Charter
theGuildCharter.flavor: They asked for a seat at the table. They were given a page of it, and took the room.
theGuildCharter.text: +2 gold for each economic Order you have in a slot, and +1 production in your capital for each.

theSynod.name: The Synod
theSynod.flavor: Everyone speaks, nobody presides, and a decision is written down regardless.
theSynod.text: +1 faith and +1 culture for each wildcard Order you have in a slot.

theHarvestSongs.name: The Harvest Songs
theHarvestSongs.flavor: The reaping song is older than the field, and older than the kingdom.
theHarvestSongs.text: Every city gains 10% of its food yield again as culture.
theHarvestSongs.note: It reads the whole harvest rather than what is left after the citizens eat: a city's surplus is decided after every percentage on it, and a card that read the surplus would be reading a figure that reads the card back.

theSaltingHouses.name: The Salting Houses
theSaltingHouses.flavor: Salt keeps the fish, the fish keeps the town, and the town keeps the salt.
theSaltingHouses.text: Coastal cities gain 10% of their food yield again as production.

theDraftingHalls.name: The Drafting Halls
theDraftingHalls.flavor: Every beam is drawn twice: once for the builder, once for the book.
theDraftingHalls.text: Cities with a Library gain 10% of their production again as science.

theGoldenScales.name: The Golden Scales
theGoldenScales.flavor: What the counting-house learns about weight, the college learns about everything else.
theGoldenScales.text: Every city gains 10% of its gold yield again as science.

theArsenalLaw.name: The Arsenal Law
theArsenalLaw.flavor: In peace the yard is quiet. Nobody in it wants peace.
theArsenalLaw.text: While you are at war, cities with a Barracks gain 15% of their production again as gold.

theCharterOfTheMarches.name: The Charter of the Marches
theCharterOfTheMarches.flavor: The furthest town is written the widest liberties, and keeps them until it is no longer the furthest.
theCharterOfTheMarches.text: Your newest city gains +2 of every yield. Founding a city grants +30 culture.

theBalladWeavers.name: The Ballad-Weavers
theBalladWeavers.flavor: Every raider who falls in the passes is worth a verse, and the verses outlast the passes.
theBalladWeavers.text: +1 culture per turn for each barbarian you have killed while this Order stands in a slot.

theBellFounders.name: The Bell-Founders
theBellFounders.flavor: A rival raises a dome; the foundry answers with a bell, and the town agrees it is the finer sound.
theBellFounders.text: +1 culture per turn for each wonder finished anywhere in the world while this Order stands in a slot.

theReliquaryRolls.name: The Reliquary Rolls
theReliquaryRolls.flavor: They served, and then they were shelved: a knuckle, a brush, a name written large.
theReliquaryRolls.text: +2 faith and +2 culture per turn for each great person you have spent while this Order stands in a slot.

theChroniclersOfTheFallen.name: The Chroniclers of the Fallen
theChroniclersOfTheFallen.flavor: The roll of the dead is read aloud on market day, and the market is fuller for it.
theChroniclersOfTheFallen.text: +1 gold per turn for each unit you have lost in battle while this Order stands in a slot.

theAlmonersBook.name: The Almoners' Book
theAlmonersBook.flavor: What the treasury spends, the almoners write down; what the almoners write down, the schools read.
theAlmonersBook.text: +1 science per turn for each 400 gold you have spent buying while this Order stands in a slot.

theCasusBelli.name: The Casus Belli
theCasusBelli.flavor: The grievance is old, the parchment is new, and the smiths were told a week ago.
theCasusBelli.text: Declaring war grants +2 combat strength to all your units and +10% production in every city, for 10 turns.
